concept_html:
Logs describe one run. A run log table lets you compare every run: which waves loaded, how many rows, how long, and which failed. It is a Delta table, append-only, with one row per pipeline run per layer.

A useful schema:

Column Type Notes
run_id STRING, not null str(uuid.uuid4()), shared by every log line of the run
pipeline_name STRING, not null nat_silver_pipeline
tracker_id, wave_id, layer STRING what the run touched
rows_processed BIGINT, not null from Delta commit metrics
status STRING, not null SUCCESS or FAILED
error_message STRING, nullable NULL on success
started_at, finished_at TIMESTAMP, not null UTC

Build the record against an explicit StructType. Your reference log_pipeline_run builds a DataFrame from a dict and lets Spark infer types. That fails on every successful run: error_message is None, and Spark raises CANNOT_DETERMINE_TYPE because it cannot infer a type from a column of only nulls. The explicit schema also rejects a wrong type, such as "12" for rows_processed, before anything is written.

Take timestamps with datetime.now(timezone.utc). datetime.utcnow() is deprecated from Python 3.12 and returns a naive datetime that carries no timezone.

Import everything you use. The reference function calls uuid and datetime without importing them, a NameError on its first run. ruff check (rule F821) catches it in CI.

Write the log record in a finally block, or in both the success and failure paths, so failed runs are logged too. A run log that only records successes cannot tell you how often the pipeline fails.

lines: import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame, SparkSession
from pyspark.sql import types as T
RUN_LOG_SCHEMA = T.StructType([
T.StructField("run_id", T.StringType(), False),
T.StructField("pipeline_name", T.StringType(), False),
T.StructField("wave_id", T.StringType(), True),
T.StructField("rows_processed", T.LongType(), False),
T.StructField("status", T.StringType(), False),
T.StructField("error_message", T.StringType(), True),
T.StructField("started_at", T.TimestampType(), False),
T.StructField("finished_at", T.TimestampType(), False),
])
def new_run_id() -> str:
"""A unique id shared by the log lines and the run log row of one run."""
return str(uuid.uuid4())
def run_record(
spark: SparkSession,
run_id: str,
pipeline_name: str,
wave_id: str | None,
rows_processed: int,
status: str,
started_at: datetime,
error_message: str | None = None,
) -> DataFrame:
"""One run log row, typed by RUN_LOG_SCHEMA."""
finished_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
row = (run_id, pipeline_name, wave_id, rows_processed, status, error_message, started_at, finished_at)
return spark.createDataFrame([row], RUN_LOG_SCHEMA)

from datetime import datetime, timezone

from pyspark.sql import DataFrame, SparkSession
from pyspark.sql import types as T

RUN_LOG_SCHEMA = T.StructType([
    T.StructField("run_id", T.StringType(), False),
    T.StructField("pipeline_name", T.StringType(), False),
    T.StructField("rows_processed", T.LongType(), False),
    T.StructField("status", T.StringType(), False),
    T.StructField("error_message", T.StringType(), True),
    T.StructField("started_at", T.TimestampType(), False),
    T.StructField("finished_at", T.TimestampType(), False),
])


def run_record(spark: SparkSession, run_id: str, pipeline_name: str, rows_processed: int, status: str, started_at: datetime, error_message: str | None = None) -> DataFrame:
    """One run log row typed by RUN_LOG_SCHEMA.

    Args:
        spark: Active session.
        run_id: Unique id of the run.
        pipeline_name: Job name.
        rows_processed: Rows written by the run.
        status: SUCCESS or FAILED.
        started_at: UTC start time.
        error_message: Error text for a failed run.

    Returns:
        A one-row DataFrame ready to append to the run log table.
    """
    finished_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    row = (run_id, pipeline_name, rows_processed, status, error_message, started_at, finished_at)
    return spark.createDataFrame([row], RUN_LOG_SCHEMA)

title: A pipeline run log table with an explicit schema
why_html:
The reference log_pipeline_run has never succeeded. It fails first with NameError: name 'uuid' is not defined. Once someone adds the imports, it fails on every successful run with CANNOT_DETERMINE_TYPE, because error_message=None is the only value in its column. The orchestrator catches that error "so logging never breaks the pipeline". Months later the team wants to show a client every load of 2025. The run log table is empty.

An explicit schema, imported names and a test that writes one record on a local SparkSession prevent all three problems.
